convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom with unknown custom indicator 'BnB' and two external .mqh includes (TradeAlgorithms.mqh, SmoothAlgorithms.mqh) containing trade management and smoothing algorithms that must be manually reimplemented in Python.

derived_values.name: Ind - main indicator buffer (buffer 1 of BnB)
Sign - signal line buffer (buffer 0 of BnB)

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MarginMode enum controls lot sizing method; LOT mode uses fixed lot fraction of 0.1

custom_logic_notes: BnB is a custom indicator with two buffers: buffer 0 (signal line) and buffer 1 (main line). Entry is crossover-based: long when Ind crosses above Sign, short when Ind crosses below Sign. Signal is evaluated on SignalBar=1 (previous completed bar) vs SignalBar+1. The crossover is detected by comparing Ind[1]>Sign[1] (prior bar state) with Ind[0]<=Sign[0] (current signal bar state). Uses SmoothAlgorithms.mqh for the T3 smoothing method (XMA_Method=MODE_T3, XPhase=15). TradeAlgorithms.mqh provides BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose, GlobalVariableDel_, CIsNewBar, LoadHistory, and GetStartBars helper functions. BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/BuyPosClose/SellPosClose boolean inputs gate which directions are allowed. Recount flag triggers re-evaluation on data recalculation.
python_conversion_notes: Must reimplement BnB indicator from source (likely uses T3 smoothing from SmoothAlgorithms.mqh). The T3 algorithm with period=14 and phase=15 needs porting. Trade management helpers (BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, etc.) from TradeAlgorithms.mqh need Python equivalents for position tracking, lot sizing, and order execution simulation. Crossover logic is straightforward: compare Ind vs Sign across two consecutive bars. Signal is only evaluated once per new bar (CIsNewBar guard) or on Recount. The MM=0.1 with LOT mode means fixed 0.1 lot sizing; other MarginMode options need implementation if used.
